import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# --- Visualization ---

# Set a clean seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a figure with two subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(14, 15), sharex=False) # sharex=False because sorting order might differ

# Sort occupations by median Sleep Duration for the first plot
# This helps in visually comparing occupations with similar sleep durations
occupation_order_duration = df.groupby('Occupation')['Sleep Duration'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index

# Plot 1: Distribution of Sleep Duration by Occupation
sns.boxplot(x='Occupation', y='Sleep Duration', data=df, ax=axes[0], order=occupation_order_duration, palette='viridis')
axes[0].set_title('Distribution of Sleep Duration Across Different Occupations', fontsize=16, pad=15)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Occupation', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45, ha='right') # Rotate labels for better readability
axes[0].grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Sort occupations by median Quality of Sleep for the second plot
# This helps in visually comparing occupations with similar sleep quality
occupation_order_quality = df.groupby('Occupation')['Quality of Sleep'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index

# Plot 2: Distribution of Quality of Sleep by Occupation
sns.boxplot(x='Occupation', y='Quality of Sleep', data=df, ax=axes[1], order=occupation_order_quality, palette='plasma')
axes[1].set_title('Distribution of Quality of Sleep Across Different Occupations', fontsize=16, pad=15)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Occupation', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10 Scale)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45, ha='right') # Rotate labels for better readability
axes[1].grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Add an overall title to the figure
fig.suptitle('Sleep Health Metrics by Occupation', fontsize=20, y=1.02)

# Adjust layout to prevent overlapping elements
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.98]) # Adjust rect to make space for suptitle

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
